subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observer or mirror mode, and what transcript visibility boundary should it enforce across agents, sessions, channels, and operators?
rationale: The current Gateway primitives make a narrow observer plausible, but exposing cross-channel transcripts changes privacy, security, retention, and public CLI/config expectations that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Read-only observer first
options.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that only shows authorized activity for a selected agent or session scope and leaves bidirectional channel mirroring out of scope.

options.title: Full bidirectional mirroring
options.body: Allow TUI and channel messages to appear across surfaces, but require explicit delivery, authorization, redaction, and upgrade policy before implementation.

options.title: No core observer mode
options.body: Keep logs, explicit session views, and future activity timelines as the supported monitoring paths and avoid a core cross-channel TUI mirror feature.

recommendation.title: Read-only observer first
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that only shows authorized activity for a selected agent or session scope and leaves bidirectional channel mirroring out of scope.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the TUI isolation change and have the clearest history on the related TUI/session visibility and policy boundary.
